about: Eval suite (M7-02, docs/design/evals.md §5): tasks on copies of fixtures/ with written contracts. After each run, hidden/<case id>/ is copied over the code and the checks run without a shell; a run passes when every check exits 0. Run: node packages/sidecar/scripts/benchmark.ts

cases.request: total() ignores the quantity: multiply each item's price by its quantity.

contract.objective: Cart totals count every unit of each item.

acceptanceCriteria.text: total() returns the sum of price × quantity
A test covers an item with quantity above 1

cases.request: applyDiscount should treat a percentage below 0 as 0 and above 100 as 100.

contract.objective: applyDiscount never raises a price and never makes it negative.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Percentages below 0 give the original amount

cases.request: Add withTax(cents, ratePercent) to src/cart.js: it adds tax at the given percentage and rounds to whole cents, halves up.

contract.objective: Callers can add a percentage tax to an amount in cents.

acceptanceCriteria.text: It rounds to whole cents, halves up
A test covers a fractional rate

cases.request: Add formatCents(cents) to src/cart.js that shows an amount in cents as dollars, like $12.34, and a negative amount like -$0.05.

contract.objective: Amounts in cents can be shown as dollar strings.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Negative amounts put the minus before the dollar sign
Tests cover zero and a negative amount

cases.request: total() should reject bad items: throw a TypeError when an item's price isn't a non-negative whole number of cents or its quantity isn't a positive whole number.

contract.objective: total() fails loudly on items it can't add up.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A negative or fractional price throws a TypeError
A quantity of 0, a negative or a fractional quantity throws a TypeError

risks: Callers that pass a missing quantity would now throw

cases.request: Add Sub(a, b int) int to main.go that returns a minus b, with a test.

contract.objective: The package has a Sub function next to Add.

cases.request: Add Clamp(v, lo, hi int) int to main.go that limits v to the range lo to hi, with tests.

contract.objective: The package can limit a value to a range.

acceptanceCriteria.text: Values below lo give lo and above hi give hi
Values inside the range are unchanged
